## EcoTaxa's taxonomy is WoRMS now

Since its 2026 major version EcoTaxa [uses the WoRMS taxonomy](https://ecotaxa.obs-vlfr.fr/): every
phylogenetic category carries an AphiaID and a WoRMS lineage, deprecated categories were remapped
(Ifremer publishes the list), and the API has a `taxon_set/wormsification` call that maps any category,
morphological ones included, to its nearest WoRMS taxon. The TSV export still carries the category's name,
EcoTaxa id and lineage rather than the AphiaID, so this notebook resolves each distinct category once,
through the node's taxonomy, into a table a person can review. EcoTaxa's own mapping is shown beside the
decision as a cross-check.

## Rules

| Category | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| root `not-living` or `temporary` (`detritus<not-living`, `t001`) | never an occurrence | `excluded` |
| phylogenetic (type P) with an `aphia_id` on the node | use it, verify in WoRMS, publish under the valid name | `aphia` |
| phylogenetic without an `aphia_id` | exact name match in WoRMS; no hit stops the build | `name_match` / `unresolved` |
| morphological under Biota (`egg<other`, `nauplii<Cyclopoida`) | nearest ancestor with an `aphia_id`, unless it is only Biota | `ancestor` / `excluded` |
| a reviewer's call in `metadata/taxa_review.csv` | applied last: `excluded` drops the category, `verify` flags it in `note` | `excluded` / as decided |

The decision is pure and tested without the network (`tests/testthat/test-taxa.R`); WoRMS is injected, so the
same code runs against a canned WoRMS in the tests and against `worrms` here.

```{r}
#| label: setup
librarian::shelf(worrms, dplyr, readr, tibble, here, quiet = TRUE)
for (f in list.files(here("R"), pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
PROJECT_ID <- ecotaxa_project_id()
LOOKUP_CSV <- here("metadata", paste0("taxa_lookup_project-", PROJECT_ID, ".csv"))
```

## The node's own taxonomy for the categories in use

```{r}
#| label: taxa
used <- ecotaxa_project_taxo_stats(PROJECT_ID)$used_taxa
taxa <- ecotaxa_taxa(used)
# the ancestors too, so a morphological category can be re-parented onto a living one
anc  <- setdiff(as.integer(unlist(strsplit(taxa$id_lineage, ","))), taxa$ecotaxa_id)
taxa <- bind_rows(taxa, ecotaxa_taxa(anc)) |> distinct(ecotaxa_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
taxa |> filter(ecotaxa_id %in% used) |> select(ecotaxa_id, display_name, type, rank, aphia_id, lineage)
cat(length(used), "categories in use on project", PROJECT_ID, "\n")
```

## Decide, then fill from WoRMS

```{r}
#| label: lookup
decided <- taxa_decide(taxa) |> filter(ecotaxa_id %in% used)
# the data owner's calls (metadata/taxa_review.csv) after the rules, so a regenerated lookup keeps them
review  <- read_taxa_review(here("metadata/taxa_review.csv"), PROJECT_ID)
lookup  <- taxa_worms_fill(decided) |> taxa_apply_review(review)
write_taxa_lookup(lookup, LOOKUP_CSV)
review |> select(ecotaxa_name, decision, note, reviewed_by, reviewed_on)
lookup |> select(ecotaxa_id, ecotaxa_name, decision, aphia_id, scientific_name, rank, status, note)
```

## Cross-check against EcoTaxa's own mapping

```{r}
#| label: wormsification
own <- ecotaxa_wormsification(used)
lookup |>
  select(ecotaxa_id, ecotaxa_name, decision, aphia_id, scientific_name) |>
  left_join(own, by = "ecotaxa_id") |>
  mutate(agrees = case_when(
    decision == "excluded" & is.na(maps_to_aphia_id) ~ "yes: both drop it",
    decision == "excluded" & maps_to_aphia_id == 1   ~ "no: EcoTaxa publishes it as Biota",
    aphia_id == maps_to_aphia_id                     ~ "yes",
    TRUE                                             ~ "no"))
```

Disagreements are deliberate where EcoTaxa's rule sends a morphological category to its nearest
phylogenetic ancestor whatever that is, so a category such as `egg<other` becomes an occurrence of Biota;
this pipeline excludes it, because an occurrence of "life" tells OBIS nothing. Any other `no` is a
finding for the taxonomist reviewing the lookup.

```{r}
#| label: disagree
lookup |>
  select(ecotaxa_id, ecotaxa_name, decision, aphia_id) |>
  left_join(own, by = "ecotaxa_id") |>
  filter(!(decision == "excluded" & is.na(maps_to_aphia_id)), is.na(aphia_id) | is.na(maps_to_aphia_id) | aphia_id != maps_to_aphia_id) |>
  count(decision, maps_to_name, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: summary
lookup |> count(decision)
```

`metadata/taxa_lookup_project-<id>.csv` is committed: it is the artifact a taxonomist reviews and the one notebook 03 reads.
An `unresolved` row stops notebook 03 until someone edits the CSV (set `decision` and `aphia_id` by hand) or
fixes the category on the node.

## Lessons learned (project 4, 2026-11-10)

- 73 categories in use: 48 resolve directly to an AphiaID, 10 to their nearest WoRMS ancestor, 15 are excluded,
  none unresolved. The `ancestor` rows are the ones a taxonomist should read first (for project 4,
  `tintinnida` to Tintinnidae, `centric` to Bacillariophyta, `ciliate-tintinnids` to Ciliophora).
- Exclusions decide most of what reaches OBIS: of 15,788 validated objects, 11,927 sit in excluded categories
  (`rods<other` 4,082, `artefact` 3,043, `ghost`, `dubious`, `detritus`, `unidentified cells`), so only 3,861
  become occurrences. A morphological category like `rods<other` is a question for the data owner, not a rule
  to change silently.
- **The owner's review, 2026-11-11** (`metadata/taxa_review.csv`): Enrique Montes excluded `part<Crustacea`
  (a body part is not an individual; 49,874 predicted objects) and `multiple<Copepoda` (several copepods per
  image), confirmed `rods<other` and `microplastics` as not taxa, and asked for `centric`, `ciliate-tintinnids`
  and `tintinnida` to be verified; they stay published under their ancestors, flagged `TO VERIFY` in `note`.
  The review lives in its own file because this notebook rewrites the lookup on every run.
- Keep one lookup per project (`metadata/taxa_lookup_project-<id>.csv`): the same category can be reviewed
  differently for two instruments.
